title: A companion text
hook: the book you'll keep reading for years: Augustine heard a child chant "take up and read", and the same book spoke next to his friend
tomorrow: how long did Ezra keep reading, and how much each day?

segments.voice: My people: Mencius began at home, and Mozi wouldn't stop at the door. That's the others page done. A new stretch now: study, and the book you'll keep.

A song comes through a neighbor's wall, half heard, and won't leave your head. Augustine heard something like that, in a garden in Milan. He was under a fig tree, crying, stuck between the life he had and the one he wanted. Then, from a house next door, a child's voice, boy or girl, he couldn't tell, chanting the same words over and over: "Take up and read; Take up and read."
screen: `A SONG THROUGH THE WALL.` → `UNDER A FIG TREE IN MILAN.` → `TAKE UP AND READ.`

segments.voice: He'd left a book where his friend was sitting, the letters of the apostle Paul. He went back, picked it up, opened it, and read in silence the first lines his eyes fell on. One of them: "But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ." He didn't read further. He didn't need to. In his Confessions he says the darkness of doubt was gone. He marked the place, closed the book, and told his friend Alypius, who was with him. Then Alypius asked to see it, and read on, past where Augustine stopped. The next line was about receiving someone weak in the faith. Alypius took that one as his own. Same book, same page, a different word for a different friend. Christians teach that scripture is living: "the word of God is quick, and powerful," as Hebrews puts it, quick meaning alive. That's one reason Christians return to the same book for a lifetime and expect it to speak again. A companion text, on your own path, is one book like that. Not the newest. The one you can hold in your hands for years, and still find a line waiting.
screen: `THE FIRST LINES HIS EYES FELL ON.` · `PUT YE ON THE LORD JESUS CHRIST.` · `ALYPIUS READS ON.` · `THE WORD OF GOD IS QUICK.` · then, large: `MY BOOK.`

segments.voice: Set the book you'd most like to keep reading in front of you, or any book you love. Look at the cover, the worn corners, the creases in the spine. Open it anywhere, let your eyes fall on one line, the way Augustine's did, and stop there.
A companion text: the one book you'll keep reading for years, the way Augustine and Alypius each found their own line in the same pages.
To keep: my book. The same pages, and a new line waiting each time. Day 1663, and study begins.

howItsDone: Christians read the Bible as a living word and return to it for a lifetime. People on many paths keep one companion text, read slowly and often, for years.

Augustine.meaning: a North African bishop and writer of the Confessions

Milan.meaning: the Italian city where Augustine's garden was

Confessions.meaning: Augustine's account of his life, written as a prayer to God

Alypius.meaning: Augustine's close friend, with him in the garden
